steps.note: Start a multi-stage event creation flow.
A title is required for a valid event and for identifying the event in the vendor portal.
Create an RFQ, the pricing stage needed for a normal vendor bid.
Apply the first available RFQ pricing template.
Add one line so the bid and counter offer have a quoted line.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet before publishing.
Commit a valid bidding schedule.
Invite the QA vendor used for the normal bid and vendor-portal check.
Publish the event so the vendor can bid.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Confirm the vendor bid was accepted.
Open the buyer comparison grid to initiate the counter offer on the normal bid.
Send the buyer's counter offer at 90 with the required remark.
Confirm the pending counter offer is recorded for the vendor's bid.
Move to the separate supplier-portal session while leaving the buyer session available.
Open the event overview where the pending counter offer is shown to the bidding vendor.
Assert that the vendor sees a counter-offer notice.
Assert that the notice includes the vendor's original quoted price.
Assert that the notice includes the buyer's offered price.
Assert that the buyer's remark is visible.
Assert that the vendor can accept the counter offer.
Assert that the vendor is also offered a reject action.
